text: When Michael was six, he asked why he could not call Helen Mummy, as other boys called their mothers, and she gently explained that she was only his auntie. <break time="0.8s" /> Since he was so eager, however, she allowed him to use the word at bedtime as a private pet name, a secret to be shared only between the two of them. <break time="0.8s" /> Michael kept the secret faithfully, but when he discovered that Helen had told her friends about it, he flew into a furious rage that astonished her. <break time="0.8s" /> Why did you tell, he cried at the end of the storm, and he declared that he would never call her Mummy again, not even at bedtime. <break time="0.8s" /> At ten, after two terms at a preparatory school, Michael came to understand the truth about his birth, and he wondered anxiously whether Helen would think less of him. <break time="0.8s" /> Far from pushing him away, Helen reassured him so tenderly that the two of them grew closer than ever, and the subject was not raised again for years. <break time="0.8s" /> Later, when he lay delirious with measles at his public school, the old question returned in his fever, and once more Helen calmed and comforted him. <break time="0.8s" /> Michael grew into a clever young man, and in the summer of 1914 he was looking forward to going up to Oxford with a scholarship in October.
